en.title: Strictly Heavier Item Set With the Fewest Items and Maximum Weight
en.description:
Split all items, by identity, into A and B, with each item in exactly one group; different items with the same weight are still separate. You need sum(A)>sum(B). First minimize the number of items in A, then, among the minimum counts, maximize the total weight of A, and output the weights of A in ascending order. B may be empty.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n and the second line contains the weights. 1≤n≤100000, 1≤arr[i]≤10000.
en.output: Output the weights of the items in A in ascending order, separated by spaces; a repeated weight is printed once per item.
en.explanation: The answers are 4 5, 5 6 and 2 2 respectively. In the third example, choosing one item only ties, so both items must go into A.
hints: Take weights in descending order until the chosen weight is strictly greater than the unchosen weight; reverse the chosen prefix to output it in ascending order.
